document.abstract: This paper presents an innovative system architecture that leverages the fast switching speed, nonlinear output response, and high optical flux threshold of the Grating Light Valve (GLV)* technology to create high-performance displays. This architecture creates a high-resolution projected image by optically scanning a linear array of GLV pixels, requiring about two thousand times fewer pixels than a 2-D panel and about one thousand times lower bandwidth than a scanned-spot approach for HDTV display. A 1080p projection display prototype based on this architecture has been developed, which displays 1920 times 1080 resolution, 30-bit color (10 bit/channel RGB) and up to 120-Hz refresh. The system receives 1080p video data at 24 or 30 frames/sec via a standard SMPTE 292M serial digital interface. While leveraging many traditional realtime video-processing techniques, several processing steps that are unique to the scanned linear architecture have been developed, including display mapping, data calibration, row/column transpose, frame rate multiply, and frame dither/refresh. The system is synchronous at 74.25 MHz.

authors.affiliation: R. W. Corrigan, B. R. Lang, D. A. LeHoty, and P. A. Alioshin are with Silicon Light Machines, Sunnyvale, CA 94089.
authors.bio: Robert Corrigan is vice-president of marketing and business development at Silicon Light Machines. In this role, Corrigan is responsible for the company's product strategy and marketing activities. Before joining SLM, he was vice-president of marketing at Stanford Telecommunications. He also served as a senior marketing manager at Apple Computer, where he was responsible for product strategy and planning for Apple's display product line. Corrigan has 13 years of marketing experience across a range of video and imaging oriented products. — Corrigan holds a B.A. from Harvard University.
authors.name: R. W. Corrigan

authors.affiliation: R. W. Corrigan, B. R. Lang, D. A. LeHoty, and P. A. Alioshin are with Silicon Light Machines, Sunnyvale, CA 94089.
authors.bio: Bruce Lang is product marketing manager for Silicon Light Machines, where he is responsible for defining and marketing the company's display products. Before joining Silicon Light Machines, he was product marketing manager at Altera Corp., where he launched several successful CPLD product families and was responsible for overall product strategy. — Lang has been involved in the semiconductor industry for ten years and has over eight years of marketing experience across a range of semiconductor and display products. A SMPTE member since 1998, Lang received a BSEE from Stanford University in 1990 and an MBA from Santa Clara University in 1996.
authors.name: B. R. Lang

authors.affiliation: R. W. Corrigan, B. R. Lang, D. A. LeHoty, and P. A. Alioshin are with Silicon Light Machines, Sunnyvale, CA 94089.
authors.bio: Dave LeHoty is a senior member of the technical staff at Silicon Light Machines (SLM) in Sunnyvale, CA, where since 1996 he has worked on algorithms, analysis, software, and hardware to connect high-definition video and D-cinema sources to SLM's Grating Light Valve (GLV) technology. His solutions support the standard HDTV gamut and the extended gamut available from laser light sources. — LeHoty holds a BSEE from Case Western Reserve University and an MSEE from Stanford University.
authors.name: D. A. LeHoty

authors.affiliation: R. W. Corrigan, B. R. Lang, D. A. LeHoty, and P. A. Alioshin are with Silicon Light Machines, Sunnyvale, CA 94089.
authors.bio: Paul Alioshin is a director of engineering at Silicon Light Machines. As the project leader for high-resolution, high-brightness display products, he is responsible for the system architecture and for ensuring that product meets the market requirements. Although he is also involved in optics, MEMS, and lasers, Alioshin's background is in high-speed digital signal processing. Before joining Echelle/Silicon Light Machines, he worked at a successful professional digital audio startup. — Alioshin holds a BSEE from the University of California at San Diego.
